predecessors.name: Duchy of Burgundy
predecessors.text: the Duchy of Burgundy, claimed by the crown in 1361 (Crown lands page) and given in apanage to Philip the Bold in 1363

successors.name: Kingdom of France
successors.text: Second Treaty of Arras, 23 December 1482: 'Burgundy's dukedom and Picardy went to France'

successors.name: House of Habsburg
successors.text: the Burgundian Netherlands, which stayed with the Habsburgs

ledger.x: 1363: Philip the Bold receives the Duchy of Burgundy in apanage and the Burgundian State begins.
30 January 1384: Louis II of Flanders dies and Philip the Bold becomes count consort of Flanders and Artois.
1384: the Free County of Burgundy (Franche-Comté) joins Flanders and Artois under Philip the Bold, as Margaret's inheritance.
1384: Nevers and Rethel come with Margaret's inheritance (joint rule with Margaret, 1384).
1429: Philip the Good incorporates Namur.
1430: Philip the Good inherits Brabant and Limburg from his cousin Philip of Saint-Pol.
1432: Philip the Good takes Hainaut, Holland, Friesland and Zeeland from Jacqueline.
20/21 September 1435: the Treaty of Arras gives Philip the Somme towns, Vermandois, Auxerre, Boulogne and Ponthieu.
1443: Philip the Good buys Luxembourg.
1463: Philip gives up some land to Louis XI.
1469: Charles the Bold buys Upper Alsace from Sigismund of Austria.
1473: Charles the Bold makes Lorraine a Burgundian protectorate.
1473: Guelders comes to Charles the Bold.
April 1474: Upper Alsace rises against Burgundian rule and the pledged lands are lost.
1475: the protectorate ends in conquest.
1475: Charles the Bold conquers the Duchy of Lorraine.
6 October 1476: René II retakes Nancy and Lorraine is lost.
January 1477: Louis XI invades the Burgundian lands after Charles's death.
23 December 1482: the Second Treaty of Arras ends the war of succession.
December 1482: Burgundy and Picardy pass to France.
December 1482: the Burgundian State ends; the dukedom goes to France and the Netherlands to the Habsburgs.

wars.name: Hundred Years' War (Burgundian phase)
wars.outcome: The Treaty of Arras (20/21 September 1435) revoked the Treaty of Troyes, made Philip recognize Charles VII and gave him the Somme towns, Vermandois, Auxerre, Boulogne and Ponthieu.

wars.name: Burgundian Wars
wars.outcome: Charles conquered Lorraine in 1475, lost Nancy to René II on 6 October 1476 and was killed at Nancy on 5 January 1477.

wars.name: War of the Burgundian Succession
wars.outcome: Louis XI overran Picardy, Artois and the duchy after Nancy; the Second Treaty of Arras (23 December 1482) gave Burgundy and Picardy to France and left the Netherlands to the Habsburgs.

certainty.note: A composite of feudal counties and duchies with no boundary survey; the Arras lines of 1435 and 1482 are treaty lines and the Netherlands/France frontier follows the counties.
